claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi is a rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy.
The initial cast-and-homogenized AlCoCrFeNi material is primarily FCC.
Standard casting and homogenization produce a conventional coarse-grained AlCoCrFeNi microstructure.
Refining the alloy to an ultrafine-grained or nanocrystalline microstructure increases grain-boundary density.
The increased grain-boundary density produces enhanced local interfacial strain fields.
Grain-boundary-associated strain fields modulate magnetic exchange interactions.
The refined microstructure and its strain fields facilitate easier magnetic-domain-wall motion or alignment.
Easier domain-wall motion in the ultrafine-grained material reduces coercivity and magnetic hysteresis relative to the coarse-grained baseline.
The ultrafine-grained microstructure enhances the magnetocaloric effect under applied fields below 1 T.
A high density of interfaces improves heat conduction and cyclic heat-exchange performance.
Ultrafine-grained AlCoCrFeNi can retain mechanical robustness relative to the coarse-grained material.
Annealing between 600°C and 800°C for durations such as 10 minutes and 2 hours can generate nanocrystalline and coarse-grained AlCoCrFeNi variants.
The intervention keeps overall alloy composition fixed while varying heat-treatment conditions.
Magnetic performance will be tested below 1 T at ambient temperature, together with cyclic heat exchange and mechanical integrity.
Coercivity and magnetic-domain-wall motion are sensitive to grain size and heat-treatment-dependent microstructure.
At fixed composition, coercivity can be tuned through quenching, heat treatment, or pressure treatment.
The proposed relationship is limited to FCC AlCoCrFeNi annealed between 600°C and 800°C over grain sizes from nanocrystalline to coarse, excluding phase transformations and severe degradation.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant magnetocaloric enhancement and hysteresis reduction, or deterioration of heat exchange or mechanical stability, would falsify the hypothesis.
